question: Does the real 956.9 kg CAD v3.0 Atom Lithography Machine with Cryomech PT420 (1.4 Hz + harmonics), cleanroom seismic floor (VC-C/E/G), cantilevered 562.66 mm Exp124 ion column, and ±10 mK room thermal swing actually meet the Exp66/Exp124 lateral placement budget (sigma_stage <= 0.50 nm, sigma_pointing <= 0.50 nm, sigma_thermal <= 0.30 nm), and what exact mechanical decoupling (k_bellows, k_braid, remote valve) + active control specifications are required for CAD v4.0?

literature_anchors.seismic_floor_vc: IEST-RP-CC012.2 / Amick et al. (VC-C=12.5 um/s, VC-E=3.1 um/s, VC-G=0.78 um/s 1/3-octave RMS velocity)
literature_anchors.pt420_vibration: Tomaru et al., Cryogenics 44 (2004) 309; Olivieri et al., RSI 88 (2017) 085109; Cryomech PT420 datasheet (1.4 Hz fundamental + harmonic comb; remote rotary valve reduces high-frequency reaction force >10x)
literature_anchors.interferometer_noise: Zygo ZMI / Attocube IDS3010 class heterodyne laser interferometer (~1.5 pm/sqrt(Hz) white floor, 0.05 nm integrated RMS)
literature_anchors.cte_materials: Zerodur (0.02 ppm/K), Invar-36 (1.2 ppm/K), 316LN SS (16.0 ppm/K), Ti-6Al-4V (8.6 ppm/K), cryogenic Si/Cu (<1e-9 /K below 4 K)

success_rule: CY1, CY2, CY4, CY6, CY7, and CY8 all PASS: coupled MDOF + Euler-Bernoulli FEM + closed-loop control proves rigid PT420 breaks budget while decoupled + active-isolated + PID/FF architecture closes sigma_stage <= 0.50 nm, sigma_pointing <= 0.50 nm, sigma_thermal <= 0.30 nm, and Exp124 sigma_total <= 3.80 nm on VC-E with stable control margins.

predictions.CY1_modal_realism: 40-element Euler-Bernoulli stepped column FEM + 6-DOF machine MDOF has positive real modes with 1st cantilevered column bending mode f_col_1 in [40, 350] Hz, pneumatic isolation mode in [1.0, 2.5] Hz, and Parseval RMS parity < 1%.
predictions.CY2_rigid_pt420_fails: Rigidly mounted PT420 (on-head rotary valve + solid Ø7 mm Cu rod 9.06 MN/m + rigid OVC bridge) exceeds sigma_stage > 50 nm open-loop and > 2.0 nm even under full closed-loop control, proving physical decoupling is mandatory.
predictions.CY3_decoupled_open_still_exceeds: Mechanical decoupling alone (remote valve + bellows 2000 N/m + OFHC braids 60 N/m, passive 1.5 Hz air springs, open-loop stage) reduces sigma_stage > 100x vs rigid yet still exceeds 0.50 nm on VC-E.
predictions.CY4_closed_loop_meets_budget_vce: Full v4.0 decoupled + active table (0.5-100 Hz) + piezo PID + 1.4 Hz harmonic feedforward (CFG4) achieves sigma_stage <= 0.50 nm and sigma_pointing <= 0.50 nm on VC-E with PM >= 45 deg, GM >= 6 dB, ||S||_inf <= 2.0.
predictions.CY5_cleanroom_floor_sensitivity: Sweeping VC-C / VC-E / VC-G shows VC-E (3.1 um/s) is the minimum cleanroom grade that comfortably clears the 0.50 nm spec under CFG4, while VC-G provides >= 1.5x additional margin.
predictions.CY6_decoupling_stiffness_envelope: 2D (k_bellows, k_braid) sweep identifies explicit CAD v4.0 upper stiffness bounds k_bellows_max and k_braid_max where sigma_stage <= 0.50 nm and sigma_pointing <= 0.50 nm hold, with k_braid sensitivity > 10x stronger than k_bellows.
predictions.CY7_thermal_drift_budget: Under ±10 mK cleanroom HVAC swing (T=900 s), a naive stainless metrology frame exceeds 0.30 nm, whereas the CAD v3.0 Zerodur + Invar-36 + cryogenic wafer island + fiducial update (t_fid <= 300 s) keeps sigma_thermal <= 0.30 nm.
predictions.CY8_exp124_total_closure: Substituting CFG4 (VC-E) computed (sigma_stage, sigma_pointing, sigma_thermal) into the Exp124 5 keV RSS placement budget preserves sigma_total <= 3.80 nm (and <= 3.674 nm target at ArchB_HiRes_Ti0p25_10ms).
